items.title: Call to Order / Roll Call
Welcome by the School Board President, Mike Wells
Changes to the Agenda
Approval of Agenda
Oral Communication

publicComments.name: Meng Zhou
publicComments.summary: Advocated for expansion of the Orion Mandarin Immersion program, presenting data on growing demand, waitlists, explosive growth of Asian families in Redwood City, and requesting the board accommodate all first-round applicants for the upcoming school year.

publicComments.name: Michelle Strobie
publicComments.summary: Advocated for the Mandarin Immersion program, presenting CAASPP data showing socioeconomically disadvantaged students in MI schools outperform peers, and requesting the board add an additional TK and K classroom to meet growing demand.

publicComments.name: Kimberly Abbey
publicComments.summary: Shared her positive personal experience as a TK parent in the MI program and urged the board to expand the program so more families can join.

publicComments.name: Wei Ji
publicComments.summary: Expressed desire to enroll his child in the Mandarin Immersion kindergarten program, explained the importance of Mandarin for their immigrant family, and urged expansion of the program to accommodate more families.

publicComments.name: Christina Lee
publicComments.summary: Shared her experience as a parent of a kindergartner who has been waitlisted at Orion MI since the start of the school year, and advocated for board investment in expanding the MI program so all interested children can access it.

publicComments.name: Saoirse Rafferty
publicComments.summary: A 5th grade MI student shared her personal academic transformation through the Mandarin Immersion program and urged the board to support all students, including those who cannot advocate for themselves, by continuing to invest in the program.

publicComments.name: Meng Zhou
publicComments.summary: Provided additional data on declining enrollment projections for Orion and reiterated the request to accommodate all first-round applicants and consider a supplemental application process.

publicComments.name: Megan O'Reilly Green
publicComments.summary: Clarified that advocacy for the MI program has been ongoing for two years by various families who were left on the waitlist, not just the new families presenting tonight.

publicComments.name: Chris Lau
publicComments.summary: Shared that he moved to Redwood City partly because of the Orion MI program and thanked the board for considering expanding it so his daughter can one day connect with her Asian heritage.

publicComments.name: Catherine Stewart
publicComments.summary: As a parent of a former MI student now at North Star, praised both programs for their strong teachers and test scores, and suggested that high waitlists and good academic results at those schools merit additional resources and expanded classroom capacity.

publicComments.name: Xingxing (Christine Liu)
publicComments.summary: As a first-generation immigrant parent who moved to Redwood City in 2019, expressed her hope to enroll her two children in the Mandarin Immersion program to preserve their heritage language.

publicComments.name: James Herbold
publicComments.summary: Echoed support for the MI program as a father of a prospective student, explaining that his wife's family in China speaks only Mandarin and that they would love for their daughter to attend the school near their home.
